t: Section 1360(f)(2) of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4101(f)(2)) is amended by striking “, but which may not exceed 50 percent of the cost of carrying out the requested revision or update”.

fable.w: This section only strikes a cap on the share of costs for a requested flood map revision or update; it is a funding and cost-share amendment. The tempting reading is that a "requested revision or update" implies state or local governments are involved in a federal decision, but the text itself creates no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Nothing here brings a party outside the federal government into a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking “, but which may not exceed 50 percent of the cost of carrying out the requested revision or update”

opus.w: The amendment only removes a limit on how much of a requested map revision's cost may be shared. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for people outside the federal government. The mention of a 'requested revision or update' may suggest outside involvement, but a request is like an application, and this text does nothing to change how that request is handled.
opus.s: is amended by striking “, but which may not exceed 50 percent of the cost of carrying out the requested revision or update”
opus.b:
**Step 1 – Analysis.** The tempting reading is that section 1360(f)(2) of the National Flood Insurance Act deals with revisions or updates to flood maps that communities ask for, so local governments seem to be part of the process. That reading fails here. This amendment only deletes a 50-percent limit on how costs are shared. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty or right to sue. A request for a revision is also closer to an application than to taking part in a federal decision.

**Step 2 – Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that removes a specific cost limitation from another statute. It does not create any requirement for the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from parties outside the federal government. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1360(f)(2) of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4101(f)(2)) is amended by striking “, but which may not exceed 50 percent of the cost of carrying out the requested revision or update”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section amends a statute related to flood insurance, it implicitly involves public participation in the broader regulatory scheme. However, the text itself is merely a technical amendment striking out a specific cost-limitation phrase. It does not establish any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties.
